errors.why: མཐའ་ཡས is the nāga king Ananta: the stock example of an attractive but unattainable purpose, the fever-curing jewel of the nāga, not an 'infinite jewel' (the note's gloss of it as irrelevant is also off).

fix.replace: the fever-curing jewel of the nāga Ananta

errors.english: just as engagement is brought about by removing misconceptions that lack purpose
errors.why: The Tibetan says the purpose brings about engagement by removing the superimposition that [the treatise] has no purpose, not 'misconceptions that lack purpose'.

errors.english: then engagement occurs through a mistaken understanding of the lack of purpose; or, if not mistaken, it results in turning away
errors.why: ལོག་པ here means 'removed/reversed': when [the notion of] purposelessness is understood to be removed one engages, if it is not removed one turns away; it does not mean 'mistaken'.

errors.english: If it were certain that the purpose of the subject matter must be stated, then as Dharmottara
errors.why: ཅི་སྟེ introduces an opposing view ('Suppose one says it is certain...'), so the Dharmottara citation and the following 'Therefore it is certain...' belong to the objector, not to the author's conclusion.

note: Follows the argument in outline but misreads the Ananta-jewel example and blurs several steps of the dialectic about the purpose of the opening statement.
Accurate rendering of the Vinaya bowl and teaching-posture rules with their origin stories.

errors.english: if one wears it during the summer or keeps it past the time for wearing such clothing
errors.why: In this context བགོ་བ is 'distribute/divide' (the summer gains distributed within the rains, kept past the robe-distribution time), not 'wear'; the same misreading recurs for the five urgent robes.

note: Sound account of the urgent-robe (atyayika) rule and the forest-dweller's robe deposit, with bgo ba read as 'wear' rather than 'distribute'.

errors.english: the object of measurement is self-awareness, which is the result
errors.why: The verse lists three items: suitability is the pramāṇa, [cognition itself] is the prameya, self-awareness is the result; the English merges prameya and result.

fix.find: the object of measurement is self-awareness, which is the result
fix.replace: the object of measurement is cognition itself, and self-awareness is the result

errors.english: those cognitions which appear as objects are not distinct from the objects even if external objects exist
errors.why: The root verse says the appearing object and the cognition are not distinct (even granting an external object), as the commentary then explains.

fix.find: those cognitions which appear as objects are not distinct from the objects even if external objects exist
fix.replace: the appearing object and the cognition are not distinct, even if external objects exist

note: Commentary portions are serviceable, but two of the Pramāṇaviniścaya root verses are mis-segmented in ways that change the doctrine.
Faithful rendering of the novice verses on householder dress and robe colours with their commentary.

errors.english: The entities of the aggregates, which are the coming and going of unlearned misconceptions
errors.why: The Tibetan says the aggregates, entities that come and go, are dependent or caused for one who has not understood the errors (viparyāsa); when the errors are understood they are not; there are no 'unlearned misconceptions' that come and go.

note: MMK 25 verses and commentary rendered correctly, apart from one garbled gloss on verse 9.

errors.english: Regarding the doubt that cognition arises only from the senses and not from sound
errors.why: The doubt is that what is known through the senses exists, but what is known from words does not; the point about existence is lost.

note: Dense lemma-gloss commentary followed reasonably well, with one misread objection.

errors.why: The reason is āśrayāsiddha because the qualified (specific) substratum is unestablished, not because the basis 'lacks differentiation'.

fix.replace: because the qualified substratum is not established

errors.english: Does one intend to establish speech itself autonomously
errors.why: The question is whether 'being a speaker' (vaktṛtva) is put forward as an independent (svatantra) reason or as a prasaṅga, not whether one proves speech.

note: Generally sound rendering of Kamalaśīla's reply on the svatantra/prasaṅga options and the smoke-fire example, with one logical term wrong.

errors.english: Two divisions based on consequence and essence within what is accepted
errors.why: The two divisions of 'accepted' rest on imputed effect- and nature-signs (as the text goes on to explain: effect-sign, nature-sign); 'consequence' is wrong and 'imputed' is dropped.

fix.replace: based on imputed effect and nature [signs]

errors.english: The explanation in the commentary (viniścaya) the Ascertainment
errors.why: རྣམ་འགྲེལ is the (Pramāṇa)vārttika, not the Viniścaya.

errors.english: because it is subject to change based only on that
errors.why: འགྱུར་བ here means 'occurring/arising' (a thesis fault that arises merely from that), not 'subject to change'; repeated later as 'changes based on that alone'.

errors.english: If the refuted is not a thesis by means of the valid cognitions themselves
errors.why: 'By the pramāṇas' qualifies 'refuted': if what is refuted by the pramāṇas is not a thesis, how is [refutation] taught as fourfold?

note: Follows the discussion of the refuted thesis, but the account of the kinds of inference-based refutation misrenders the technical terms and cites the wrong treatise.
Faithful verse rendering of the Tibetan of the peacock-queen episode; the interleaved Sanskrit is correctly left aside.
